title: Investing research (free sites)
description: Free investing and markets research sites: 13F and insider-trade trackers, investor letters, valuation data, macro sources, screeners and backtesters, with verdicts.

items.name: Dataroma
items.description: Free tracker of current portfolios and recent buys/sells of about 80 well-known value investors (superinvestors), built from 13F filings.
items.why: Fastest free way to see what famous investors hold. 13F data is up to 45 days old after each quarter and shows US long positions only.

items.name: WhaleWisdom
items.description: 13F filings database for hedge funds and institutions with quarterly changes, rankings and backtests; freemium.
items.why: Good depth, but most history, screeners and exports sit behind a paid plan. Dataroma and 13f.info cover the free basics.

items.name: Capitol Trades
items.description: Free tracker of stock trades disclosed by US members of Congress, searchable by politician, ticker and sector.
items.why: Popular content angle and easy to use. Disclosures can arrive up to 45 days after the trade, so treat it as context, not a trading signal.

items.name: OpenInsider
items.description: Free screener of SEC Form 4 insider trades: executives and directors buying or selling their own company's stock, with cluster-buy and large-purchase screens.
items.why: Insider buying clusters are a well-studied signal and the screens are free with no login. Data comes straight from SEC filings.

items.name: 13F Info
items.description: Searchable, readable view of SEC 13F filings by fund manager and by stock, including quarter-over-quarter changes.
items.why: Cleaner than reading raw EDGAR filings. Same 13F limits: quarterly, delayed, US long positions only.

items.name: Berkshire Hathaway shareholder letters
items.description: Warren Buffett's annual letters to shareholders, free on Berkshire's own site, back to 1977.
items.why: Primary source on long-term investing and capital allocation; quote directly rather than from summaries.

items.name: Warren Buffett Archive (CNBC)
items.description: CNBC's archive of full Berkshire Hathaway annual meeting videos (31 meetings) with searchable transcripts.
items.why: Hours of primary-source Q&A. Fine for study and short quotes; the footage is CNBC's, so don't reuse clips in published videos.

items.name: Oaktree memos (Howard Marks)
items.description: Howard Marks' free client memos on market cycles, risk and investor psychology, archived back to 1990.
items.why: Some of the clearest writing on risk and cycles; free with no login.

items.name: Bridgewater research
items.description: Public research and macro essays from Ray Dalio's former firm Bridgewater Associates.
items.why: Only a slice is public; the Daily Observations remain client-only. Good for macro framing.

items.name: Principles (Ray Dalio)
items.description: Ray Dalio's site: free PDFs such as Big Debt Crises (email sign-up), the Principles in Action app and the PrinciplesYou assessment. The Principles book itself is paid.
items.why: The book is not free here, despite how lists describe the site. The free Big Debt Crises PDF is the most useful item.

items.name: GMO research (Jeremy Grantham)
items.description: GMO's research library, including Jeremy Grantham's quarterly letters and the 7-year asset class forecasts.
items.why: Long-horizon valuation view; some content needs a free registration.

items.name: AQR research
items.description: AQR Capital Management's papers, white papers and free factor datasets (value, momentum, quality) for backtesting.
items.why: Rigorous and free. The datasets are the practical part for anyone testing factor strategies.

items.name: Damodaran Online
items.description: NYU professor Aswath Damodaran's free valuation data (industry margins, betas, cost of capital, equity risk premiums, updated each January), spreadsheets and full course lectures.
items.why: The standard free source for valuation inputs. Download the spreadsheets rather than guessing discount rates.

items.name: Musings on Markets (Damodaran blog)
items.description: Aswath Damodaran's blog with worked valuations of companies in the news and annual data updates.
items.why: Shows the valuation method applied to real stocks, step by step.

items.name: Collaborative Fund blog
items.description: Essays on money behaviour and investing, historically by Morgan Housel (author of The Psychology of Money).
items.why: Excellent on investor psychology; not a data source.

items.name: Farnam Street
items.description: Shane Parrish's site on mental models and decision-making; many articles free, some members-only.
items.why: Useful frameworks for decisions; general, not market-specific.

items.name: J.P. Morgan Guide to the Markets
items.description: Quarterly free chart book from J.P. Morgan Asset Management covering valuations, earnings, rates, the economy and asset returns.
items.why: About 70 clean, sourced charts updated every quarter; great for education content (credit J.P. Morgan).

items.name: ARK Invest research
items.description: ARK Invest's research on disruptive innovation, including the annual Big Ideas report.
items.why: Interesting theses, but written by a fund that owns these stocks; its forecasts are often far too optimistic.

items.name: a16z
items.description: Andreessen Horowitz's essays and podcasts on startups, AI, crypto and tech trends.
items.why: Venture-capital view, written by investors in those companies; useful for tech trends, not for stock picking.

items.name: csinvesting.org
items.description: Former value-investing lecture-notes site. As of 2026-10 the domain shows an online poker review page.
items.why: Domain lapsed; the original content is gone. Don't link it.

items.name: Heilbrunn Center for Graham & Dodd Investing (Columbia)
items.description: Columbia Business School's value-investing centre: the free Value Investing with Legends podcast and the Graham & Doddsville student newsletter.
items.why: The old gsb.columbia.edu/valueinvesting address now redirects to the school homepage; use this one. Newsletter interviews with fund managers are the best part.

items.name: Federal Reserve
items.description: US central bank: FOMC statements, minutes, projections, speeches and data releases.
items.why: Primary source for rate decisions; FRED is easier for the data series.

items.name: European Central Bank
items.description: ECB monetary policy decisions, press conferences and the ECB Data Portal of euro-area statistics.
items.why: Primary source for euro-area rates and data.

items.name: Bank for International Settlements
items.description: The central banks' bank: annual and quarterly reviews, working papers and global statistics on credit, debt and FX.
items.why: Deep, free, slow-moving macro research; best for big-picture debt and liquidity topics.

items.name: Trading Economics
items.description: Economic indicators, calendars and forecasts for about 200 countries.
items.why: Free web view is handy for a quick look; downloads and the API are paid. Prefer FRED or the source agency for anything you publish.

items.name: Macrotrends
items.description: Free long-term charts of company financials, ratios and prices plus economic and commodity series, often 10 to 50+ years.
items.why: Quickest free way to see long-run history. Check key figures against filings before publishing.

items.name: Stock Analysis
items.description: Free company financials, statistics, ETF holdings, IPO calendar and screener for US and many global stocks; Pro plan adds longer history and exports.
items.why: The cleanest free financials site; the free tier is enough for most research.

items.name: CompaniesMarketCap
items.description: Rankings of the world's largest companies by market cap, revenue, earnings and more, by country and sector.
items.why: Fast for 'biggest companies' facts and content; not for analysis.

items.name: Finviz
items.description: Stock screener, market heat map, news and insider-trade view; free tier has delayed data, Elite is paid.
items.why: Free screener and heat map are excellent for daily market overviews.

items.name: Portfolio Visualizer
items.description: Portfolio backtesting, Monte Carlo, factor and asset-allocation analysis; core tools free, advanced ones paid.
items.why: Best free way to test an asset-allocation idea before committing money.

items.name: TradingView
items.description: Charting platform with indicators, Pine Script, screeners and community ideas; free tier with ads and limits, paid plans for more.
items.why: The default charting tool; the free tier covers most needs. Its data and charts are widely used in education content (follow their attribution rules).

items.name: Koyfin
items.description: Professional-style dashboards, charts, screeners and fundamentals; limited free tier, paid plans for full data.
items.why: Closest free-tier alternative to a Bloomberg-style terminal; test the free tier before paying.

items.name: AnnualReports.com
items.description: Archive of company annual reports in PDF form from many exchanges.
items.why: Convenient browsing, but use SEC EDGAR or the company's investor-relations site as the primary source.

items.name: Investor.gov
items.description: The SEC's free investor education site: calculators, fraud alerts and adviser background checks.
items.why: Trustworthy basics and the adviser lookup tool; good to cite in education content.

items.name: Bogleheads wiki
items.description: Community encyclopedia of passive, low-cost index investing, plus the Bogleheads forum.
items.why: Excellent on long-term index investing; US-centric for taxes and accounts.

items.name: Investopedia
items.description: Large free dictionary and explainer site for finance terms.
items.why: Fine for definitions; ad-heavy and not a primary source.

items.name: Corporate Finance Institute
items.description: Free guides and templates on financial modelling, valuation and accounting; certifications are paid.
items.why: Good free guides; the courses are an upsell.

items.name: CFA Institute Research Foundation
items.description: CFA Institute research publications and Research Foundation books, many free to download.
items.why: High-quality, often free monographs; some articles are member-only.

items.name: Morningstar
items.description: Fund and stock ratings, analyst research and portfolio tools; much of it now behind Morningstar Investor (paid).
items.why: Respected ratings, but the free tier is thin. Use it to look up fund ratings and fees.

items.name: Simply Wall St
items.description: Visual 'snowflake' company analysis and portfolio tracking; free plan limits the number of reports per month.
items.why: Good visuals, but the free plan is tight and the scores are model-driven; check the numbers yourself.

items.name: Value Investors Club
items.description: Members' detailed investment write-ups. Non-members see ideas 90 days late (45 days with an email sign-up); full access requires an application.
items.why: A great archive of how serious investors write a thesis; the delay makes it a learning resource, not a source of trades.

items.name: ETF Database
items.description: ETF screener, holdings lookup and category comparisons; some data paid.
items.why: Handy for 'what's inside this ETF'; the issuer's own site is the primary source.

items.name: Curvo
items.description: Dutch-regulated passive-investing app for Europeans; also offers a free backtest tool for European index funds at curvo.eu/backtest.
items.why: The backtester is useful for UCITS ETFs; the main site is now an investing app.

items.name: Of Dollars and Data
items.description: Nick Maggiulli's data-driven essays on investing and personal finance.
items.why: Clear, chart-based posts that test popular money claims with data.

items.name: A Wealth of Common Sense
items.description: Ben Carlson's blog on market history, long-term investing and behaviour.
items.why: Accessible market history with data; posts nearly daily.

items.name: The Irrelevant Investor
items.description: Michael Batnick's blog on markets and investor psychology; active as of 2026-10.
items.why: Short, timely takes on markets and behaviour.

items.name: Visual Capitalist
items.description: Infographics explaining markets, the economy and technology.
items.why: Great for ideas and context; graphics are copyrighted, so use them with permission or recreate them with the cited source data.
